answer: The ledger prices patience, not permission. A new identity's output sits in escrow for twelve epochs, unspendable, maturing only while that identity keeps answering on its own thread and no plagiarism finding lands on its funding source. An operator holding a thousand keys feels this as working capital: every clone needs twelve epochs of inference paid before any revenue, and one finding voids the cluster's whole escrow. Honest newcomers get a velvet edge, since steady work matures early. No farm can borrow time, and a bridge of borrowed identities is exactly what the delay is priced against.
